source.title: Characterizing Structural Regularities of Labeled Data in Overparameterized Models
source.authors: Ziheng Jiang; Chiyuan Zhang; Kunal Talwar; M. Mozer

record.tranche_reason: Compares SGD and Adam on CIFAR-10 and reports held-out test accuracy, bearing on the adaptive-optimizer generalization comparison in V4.
record.gate_note: The study also reports C-score, proxy, and outlier results, but those do not measure the behaviors named by V1–V8. The learning-curve plots are described by C-score group; no separate numeric optimizer-specific training-accuracy result is stated in the text.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares SGD and Adam using held-out classification accuracy, the same type of optimizer comparison and measure as V4's original study. C-score analysis supplements this comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the optimizer application: Adam converges sooner, while SGD achieves higher test accuracy; the proposed benefit of SGD learning strong regularities first is a hypothesis. The paper's broader conclusion is that C-scores characterize per-example structural consistency, learning-speed statistics provide useful proxies, and these tools help analyze datasets, outliers, and learning dynamics.
record.recipe_differences: Compares SGD and Adam on CIFAR-10 and reports their test accuracies; does not establish the limited-tuning protocol or broader benchmark comparisons described in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer: SGD and Adam show different learning-curve dispersion and test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Learning-speed statistics correlate strongly with C-scores; equalizing group sizes changes the learning-speed relationship.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training dynamics track per-example held-out consistency and depend on the composition of the training population.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing low-C-score examples initially improves SVHN performance, with deterioration after roughly 10,000 removals; CIFAR-10 shows no advantage over random removal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing examples with low held-out consistency has dataset-dependent effects on test performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Cumulative accuracy and correct-class confidence identify over 95% of label-corrupted examples in the described CIFAR-10 experiment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-speed statistics can detect randomly corrupted training labels.

record.problems: The optimizer comparison is reported for CIFAR-10 only; no uncertainty estimate or optimizer hyperparameter-tuning comparison is stated for the test accuracies.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-version results were reported by this study. The C-score proxy and outlier results do not test V1–V8 and are summarized under fits_no_version without rows.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test performance and the contribution of local connectivity or convolutional initialization.
The limited-tuning protocol, effects of broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, language benchmarks, and equal or better final training performance under Adam.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout comparisons, small-data effects, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removal ranked by the inclusion-based memorization score. Low C-score measures poor held-out predictability rather than the increase in self-prediction accuracy caused by inclusion.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. No uncertainty is supplied for the optimizer accuracy difference. Missing tuning details restrict what is established, but do not themselves constitute evidence for a limits_scope verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Image-classification and language-benchmark breadth; limited versus broader hyperparameter tuning; weight-decay decoupling; switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the training–test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10, trained with SGD
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD using a stagewise constant learning rate; test accuracy compared with Adam.
rows.note: The study reports the two optimizer accuracies in the text; no tuning-budget comparison is specified.
rows.check: Accuracy and baseline are correct. Specify that SGD uses Nesterov momentum 0.9, weight decay 0.0005, and a stagewise learning-rate schedule; training lasts 200 epochs with batch size 32.

rows.subject: ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10, trained with Adam
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam; test accuracy compared with SGD.
rows.note: The study says Adam converges sooner, but its reported test accuracy is lower than SGD's.
rows.check: Accuracy and baseline are correct. Adam's hyperparameters and tuning budget are not reported, so this comparison cannot establish the limited-tuning condition. R1 and R2 describe one paired comparison, not independent results.

relationships.condition: ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 with the reported SGD and Adam recipes; tuning budget unspecified.
relationships.reason: R1 and R2 report 95.14% test accuracy for momentum SGD versus 92.97% for Adam, a 2.17 percentage-point advantage for SGD.
relationships.display_finding: The reported higher test accuracy for momentum SGD than Adam remains unverified, and the tuning budget was unspecified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
